description: Updates for every pinned dependency: Python (uv.lock), the UI and the website (npm), base images by digest, Debian packages in the Dockerfile and GitHub Actions by commit. A release waits two weeks before it is proposed, except where no release date exists (see the rules). The project's own image in the compose templates is left alone.

packageRules.description: Images: Docker Hub dates a release by the last push of its tag, and the official images are pushed again every few days, so two weeks never pass; GHCR gives no date at all. Without a date Renovate holds an update for good, and the base image would keep outdated Debian packages. They come without the wait, as pull requests that are tested before the merge.

Debian packages: looked up in the release and in its security archive (merged), so a security update shows before the next point release. They have no release date either, and a pinned version leaves the archive with the next update of the package.
uv waits the two weeks itself (exclude-newer in pyproject.toml), also when it rewrites uv.lock in the lock file maintenance, which has no release dates.

A new Python or Node.js version changes the runtime for all code and dependencies at once: it waits for approval on the dependency dashboard and is then done as one change (base image, required version, lint and type check targets). Digests and patches come as usual.
